prose_updates.tldr: The target is a fixed finite aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the target-indexed period-by-period conditional restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna. The observed-law restriction rows admit a deterministic finite basis, whose standardized residual vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) generates the entire tangent orthocomplement. Projecting a denominator-corrected reference gradient with \(K_P(X)^\dagger\) gives the full canonical gradient and information bound, with redundancy handled in the Moore--Penrose quotient. The conditional loading \(b^\star(X)\) remains the optimum only inside the smaller aggregate pairwise-score family. Their variance difference is the squared projection onto the period-specific normal directions omitted by that family, and it vanishes exactly when the aggregate optimum satisfies the complete conditional projection equation. The cross-fitted and gap-estimation maps are correspondingly redefined to use the complete normal vector; their downstream limit theorems must be revalidated against the new first-stage maps.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorems 4.1--4.2 and Remark 4.6) establish identification, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and constant componentwise weighting, but do not exhaust the observed tangent space of the overidentified period-specific DDD model. Staggered-DiD efficiency results do not supply the DDD full-data extension or the coupled eligibility-gap tangent normal.
project_justification.niche: Eligibility and staggered adoption create simultaneous conditional restrictions for individual periods. Cumulative clean-comparison contrasts span only part of their normal space when targets cover multiple periods, so full efficiency requires a separate period-specific projection with shared-cell covariance retained.
project_justification.fill: The note constructs a finite independent basis of every observable period-specific restriction, proves from observable equivalence that its measurable multiples exhaust the tangent orthocomplement, and derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection. It separately identifies the aggregate pairwise-score optimum and gives an exact nonnegative decomposition between its variance and the information bound. Estimator and diagnostic definitions now use the complete normal vector; asymptotic attainment and gap inference are stated only after their revised rank and nuisance remainders are verified.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates retained cell propensities, one-step outcome regressions, the denominator-corrected reference gradient, and the conditional moments \(K_P(X)=E[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}Z_P^{\mathrm{per}\prime}\mid X]\) and \(r_P(X)=E[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\psi_P^0\mid X]\). Eigenvalue thresholding is applied to the complete-normal covariance. The aggregate covariance \(\Gamma_P(X)\) and loading \(b^\star(X)\) remain relevant for comparator decomposition, not as substitutes for the full canonical correction.

prose_updates.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorems 4.1--4.2 and Remark 4.6) provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise weighting benchmark. The result here differs by deriving the complete observed tangent normal for all target-indexed period-specific DDD restrictions and projecting a denominator-corrected aggregate gradient onto it. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Theorems 3.2 and 4.1) provide the closest conditional efficiency and attainment results for staggered DiD, but their model does not imply the DDD full-data extension or the eligibility-gap tangent calculation. Chen and Xie (2026) motivate keeping structural identification distinct from observed-law tangent exhaustion. Newey (2001) informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry, while the range inclusion, quotient projection, and aggregate-to-full variance decomposition used here are proved directly. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025) cover just-identified DDD influence functions; no equivalence is claimed without matching their observed tangent restrictions. The bounded binary construction retains the exact \(3/512\) constant-versus-aggregate gain only in its stated architecture, where the aggregate and complete normal closures coincide.
prose_updates.interpretation: There are two distinct precision questions. Conditional generalized least squares across cumulative pairwise scores produces \(\phi_{\mathrm{agg}}\), and no other feasible loading of those scores has smaller variance. The semiparametric model contains additional period-specific restriction normals, so the actual canonical gradient is \(\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\psi^0-r'K^\dagger Z^{\mathrm{per}}\). The observable conditional equation \(E[Z^{\mathrm{per}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg}}\mid X]=0\) says exactly when the first optimization has already used all information relevant to the chosen aggregate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The canonical-gradient theorem is pointwise at an interior law and does not require the complete-normal covariance to be nonsingular or of constant rank for the population projection. Statistical attainment is a separate problem: the revised cross-fitted estimator must control estimation of both \(K_P\) and \(r_P\), and rank changes can make the Moore--Penrose map nonregular. The existing aggregate covariance and loading rates do not automatically constitute those full-normal rates outside a fixed-support, locally fixed-rank regime. The gap-inference theorem likewise requires revalidation after replacing the projected-score sieve and differentiating the denominator-corrected covariance and complete-normal projection.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The efficiency result applies to a fixed finite horizon and target set, at interior observed laws satisfying the complete target-indexed period-specific conditional DDD equalities and admitting an OVS full-data extension. It proves a pointwise canonical gradient and bound. Singular or redundant complete-normal coordinates are allowed at the population level because only the fitted projection is identified. Uniform inference across rank-changing laws is not claimed. The aggregate loading \(b^\star(X)\), the OVS loading, and the best joint constant loading are not called semiparametrically efficient unless they satisfy the complete period-specific projection equation. Pointwise cross-fitted attainment and efficiency-gap Wald inference remain subject to separate verification of the revised full-normal first-stage and local-rank conditions. The \(3/512\) binary gain remains an aggregate-versus-constant result and coincides with a full-efficiency comparison only in the certified architecture where the two normal closures coincide.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem delivers the full information bound by proving that a finite period-specific normal vector generates the entire tangent orthocomplement and by projecting with a singular-safe conditional operator.
statement_notes.gap: Published staggered-DDD weighting results optimize within constant pairwise-score combinations; they do not establish the observed tangent space generated by all conditional period-specific eligibility-gap restrictions.
statement_notes.consumer: The result supplies the correct efficiency benchmark and two separate diagnostics: aggregate loading optimality and equality of the aggregate optimum with the full bound.
